evidence: app/package.json:11 — 'nitro': '^3.0.261029-rc', the production server runtime is an RC build published Oct 29 2026 (stable line is 2.13.5)
app/vite.config.ts:4 — nitro() Vite plugin wired into the build, the RC is central to every production request
app/package.json:8-10 — @solidjs/start 2.1.0 (stable since Aug 2026, 2.1.0 itself a week old) and vite ^8.0.0 (stable since Mar 2026), both required by SolidStart v2
app/src/routes/index.tsx:1-3, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:1-3 — all app code uses long-stable solid-js/@solidjs/router APIs only; no createAsync/cache/query/action/islands
reach.rationale: One genuine RC (Nitro v3) sits in a central place — the production server — plus a recently-stable framework (SolidStart v2, ~3 months) and a week-old minor (2.1.0). That is exactly 'one or two recently-unstable APIs in central places', though nothing in the app's own source is experimental.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:4 — the entire Nitro-specific surface in the build is a single plugin line
app/src/routes/api-proxy/[...path].ts:1-23 — one of only two Nitro-facing handlers, using the documented APIEvent contract and web-standard Request/Response, trivially portable
app/src/routes/media/[...path].ts:1-19 — second handler, same standard shape; everything else in src/ is plain Solid APIs
grep app/src for unstable_|experimental_ — zero matches; no experimental config flags anywhere
containment.rationale: The RC's code footprint is one config line plus two small catch-all handlers written against web-standard Request/Response and SolidStart's documented APIEvent, so a v3 API shift before GA would touch three files. Only the unavoidable fact that Nitro is the runtime itself keeps this from a 5.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:1-6 — solidStart() + nitro() is verbatim the pattern in SolidStart v2's stable docs (docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/guides/deployment-plugins); the Nitro v2 bridge is deprecated, so v3-rc is the only supported Node deploy path

app/package.json:5-6 — 'vite dev/build' and 'node .output/server/index.mjs' scripts satisfy the SPEC.md requirement of npm start serving the production build on $PORT; Nitro v3 is required for that output
app/vite.config.ts:5 — ssr:false / devOverlay:false are documented stable options (docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/reference/config/solid-start), not experimental flags
app/src/lib/api.ts:18-37 — client fetching via createResource + a caching proxy route rather than newer/experimental data APIs; the new stack buys a working prod deploy, not novelty
justification.rationale: Every 'new' dependency is mandated: SolidStart v2 requires Vite 8, and its stable docs prescribe Nitro v3's vite plugin for Node deployment, which the spec's npm-start requirement needs. The app even avoids newer SolidStart data APIs in favor of long-stable createResource — no gratuitous adoption anywhere.

findings.issue: The production server runtime 'nitro' is pinned to a release-candidate channel (3.0.261029-rc, published 2026-10-29). Nitro v3 has shipped breaking changes between each pre-release ('Upgrading from Beta' notes), and a caret range (^3.0.261029-rc) will silently jump to whatever 3.x is current on fresh installs, including breaking RC-to-RC changes.
findings.suggestion: Keep the committed package-lock.json authoritative for installs, pin the exact RC in CI, and schedule an upgrade check when Nitro 3.0 GA lands; note the risk in the README for future maintainers.

findings.issue: @solidjs/start 2.1.0 was published 2026-10-22 (about a week before review) and SolidStart v2 itself was only declared stable on 2026-08-04, so the app rides the very front edge of the stable line.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable given the ecosystem situation, but consider pinning to the last 2.0.x patch if regressions appear, and watch the solid-start changelog for the first weeks.

findings.issue: The nitro() plugin instance is the single point where a future Nitro v3 GA rename/option change would break the build, and it is not documented in the repo.
findings.suggestion: A one-line comment or README note stating that the nitro() plugin is used solely to produce the Node server output would make the swap (e.g. to another deployment plugin) self-evident.

summary: The app's own source uses exclusively long-stable Solid, router and meta APIs; the only genuinely unstable piece is Nitro v3, currently an RC and the production server runtime. That RC is exactly what SolidStart v2's stable documentation prescribes for Node deployment, so its adoption is justified and confined to one config line plus two web-standard API handlers. Risk is moderate and procedural: watch for breaking changes as Nitro 3 goes GA, with package-lock.json already mitigating surprise upgrades.
